title: Drift of electrons
back: Electrons within v_d Δt cross the section in Δt, so I = neAv_d.

title: Resistivity against temperature
back: Metal: ρ rises (τ falls). Semiconductor: ρ falls (more carriers).

title: Cell with internal resistance
back: I = ε/(R + r); terminal voltage V = ε − Ir while discharging, ε + Ir while charging.

title: Two-loop circuit
back: Junction: I₂ = I₁ + I₃. Loops give the rest; a negative current flows the other way.

title: Wheatstone bridge
back: Balanced when the galvanometer reads zero: P/Q = R/S.

title: Current and drift velocity
back: Drift speed is about 10⁻⁴ m/s; the signal travels at nearly c.

title: Resistivity from the drift model
back: Depends on material and temperature, never on length or area.

title: Temperature dependence of ρ
back: Metals: α > 0. Nichrome, manganin: very small α.

title: Terminal voltage
back: Equals ε only when no current is drawn.

title: Cells in parallel
back: Series: emfs and internal resistances simply add.

title: Wheatstone bridge balance
legend: balance = no current through the galvanometer
back: Independent of the cell and galvanometer resistance: a null method.

title: What do Kirchhoff’s rules conserve?
back: "Junction pe charge, loop pe energy": junction rule = charge conservation; loop rule = energy conservation.
